messages:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing we treat large refactors as an "interleaving cutover" rather than a single big-bang migration. idea: let old and new implementations coexist with a bounded 'debt escrow' for behavioral gaps. looking for guardrail feedback.
ben: sounds useful. can you outline the lifecycle for an escrow item?
sanjay: love avoiding big bangs. operational question: how do we prevent tenant bleed when a migration is partially live? per-tenant flags?
maria: yes, per-tenant flags + traffic-routing. lifecycle sketch: 1) implement new adapter behind flag, 2) canary small traffic slice, 3) automated observability gates, 4) promote to wider traffic or rollback, 5) create debt-paydown task for any remaining adapter work.
alex: backlog control is key. propose an SLA: escrow items auto-escalate after X days.
maria: proposal: debt escrow queue with max_age=30d, review_deadline=14d. owners at 14d must pick resolve|defer|schedule.
karen: product note: some customers need compliance hold. policy must support manual holds per tenant.
ben: can we express the guardrails as a small policy file? e.g.:
```
cutover_policy:
  max_escrow_days: 30
  review_deadline_days: 14
  observability_gates:
    p50_latency_delta_percent: 10
    error_rate_delta_percent: 0.5
  canary_steps: [1, 5, 20]
  manual_holds_allowed: true
```
ben: what auto-fail signals? p95 regression? error spike? cache hit regression?
sanjay: cache miss tail & KV-hit-rate are big cost vectors — include those.
maria: agreed. required gates: p95 latency, error rate, cache_hit_ratio. require 2 consecutive passing canary windows to promote. failing any gate -> rollback and ephemeral undo.
alex: infra-wise we'll need flags-as-code + migration tags so we can query outstanding migrations programmatically.
maria: yep. tag flags with migration_id and metadata: owner, ticket, estimate.
ben: ownership question: who runs the escrow queue? service team or infra?
sanjay: service team owns the migration content; infra owns routing, tooling, and enforcement. ops ensures no orphaned items.
maria: exactly. add owner metadata (migration_id, owner, ticket_link, estimated_effort, depends_on).
akex: typo: alex: can we add a CLI to inspect & act on escrow items? `ri escrow list --stale`?
maria: yes — add to eng-toolbelt.
karen: rollout cadence — allow multiple concurrent migrations but cap concurrency at runtime to avoid resource jams. start with cap=3 per node.
ben: dependency graph concern: migration B depending on A — need blocking semantics to avoid partial exposure.
maria: add depends_on field and CI graph check. CI rejects cycles.
alex: metrics to track paydown: escrow_count, avg_time_in_escrow, resolved_per_week. dashboard pls.
karen: product will want outstanding-migrations by tenant + compliance hold state.
maria: implementation plan: week1: simple escrow store + flags-as-code tagging + CLI. week2: canary runner + observability gates. week3: soft rollout on low-risk service, iterate.
sanjay: rollback playbook thoughts: automated rollback + manual runbook. need cache invalidation strategy to avoid stray reads.
ben: targeted invalidation by migration tag instead of full flush — less noisy.
maria: good — we'll implement targeted invalidation and garbage collection.
deploy-bot: Canary started migration=mig-2026-042; 1% traffic -> new-adapter. logs: https://ci.internal/1234 (canary_id=can-789)
alex: monitoring shows a small error blip +0.2% then back to baseline. passing gates for now. :thumbsup:
karen: remind: manual holds list for compliance tenants — maria can you add to dashboard?
maria: will add hold-list and per-tenant status. assigning tasks: @sanjay escrow store + gc, @alex CLI + flags-as-code integration, @ben dashboard widgets.
sanjay: will open tracker and start prototyping today.
ben: adding dashboard ticket.
maria: thanks all. follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30. if blockers, ping here. :coffee:
